title: Microsoft Teams: pop out the sign language interpreter video in meetings
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned rollout, user steps and absence of a feature-specific admin policy. The documented IP video path and PowerShell call are supported, but the path should acknowledge Microsoft's alternative navigation and newer setting label.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: The accessibility guide ties enabling IP video to interpreters' ability to share an IP video feed in Teams meetings.
claims.quote: Give sign language interpreters the ability to share IP video feed during Microsoft Teams meetings so they can communicate with users who are deaf or hard of hearing.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The accessibility guide documents Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Audio & video > IP video.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Meetings, and then select Meeting policies. ... Select the policy you want to modify. ... Go to the Audio & video section. ... Check that IP video is turned On
claims.fix: Keep the cited path, but add: 'The accessibility guide says users of Unified Policies & Settings management find these options under Settings & Policies. The audio and video policy article calls IP video "Video conferencing": https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video.'

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowIPVideo $true to allow video sharing.
claims.quote: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet allows administrators to update existing meeting policies ... -AllowIPVideo: ... Set this to TRUE to allow the user to share their video. ... -Identity: Specify the name of the policy being created.
